holding_summary: A landlord executing on a judgment for rent cannot levy on and sell the goods of a stranger found on the demised premises; a new legal principle may be raised on a motion for judgment n.o.v. even if not argued at trial.
notes: Landlord-tenant execution/distress dispute over a leased soda fountain (chattel of a stranger); no bearing on letting of rooms/dwellings or lodging regulation.

holding_summary: A landlord whose land is in a tenant's exclusive possession may still maintain trespass against a telephone company for injury to the reversion, such as destruction of trees.
notes: Trespass/reversion dispute involving farmland and a telephone line; tenancy mentioned only to establish standing to sue, no bearing on letting of rooms or lodging.

holding_summary: A surety who bonded a tenant's distrained household goods remained liable on the bond notwithstanding a bankruptcy trustee's disclaimer of other distrained property (hearses/casket wagon) held by the tenant as bailee.
notes: Landlord distress for rent, surety bond, and bailment of business chattels; no bearing on letting of rooms/dwellings or lodging.

holding_summary: A covenant in leases of company-owned dwelling houses restricting use of the private access way to ingress/egress did not bar delivery of goods ordered by tenants, but did bar use of the way to solicit orders from other tenants once posted under the Act of 1905.
notes: Leased company dwelling houses and private-way access covenant/posted-land trespass; tenants are ordinary lessees of company houses, not lodgers/boarders, and the dispute is about the way, not the letting itself.

holding_summary: The orphans' court had jurisdiction over a tenant-by-curtesy's partition petition; adverse possession claimed by cotenants was insufficient to bar partition, and an inquest's unequal-value allotment was set aside.
notes: Estate partition and tenancy-by-curtesy dispute; unrelated to letting of rooms/dwellings or lodging regulation.

holding_summary: Where a licensee built a boundary wall that mistakenly encroached beyond the licensed line, equity ordered the wall relocated to the agreed line rather than wholly removed and rebuilt.
notes: License to build a party wall on neighboring land, encroachment dispute; not about occupancy of dwellings/rooms for pay.

holding_summary: Where a real estate broker's employment was non-exclusive and commissions were conditioned on procuring a signed lease and down payment, the broker was not entitled to commission merely for bringing landlord and prospective tenant together.
notes: Broker-commission dispute over a five-year commercial lease of storefront premises to an ice cream company; commercial letting, not householder short-term room/lodging letting.

holding_summary: A consignment agreement under which goods were delivered to a retail dealer in trust to sell, without intent to pass title and with no concealment of its nature, constituted a valid bailment and was not constructively fraudulent against creditors.
notes: Bailment/consignment of watch cases in a creditor's interpleader action; unrelated to occupancy of dwellings.

holding_summary: A borough ordinance requiring a license fee for hawkers, peddlers, and house-to-house solicitors was a reasonable and valid exercise of the police power, not a prohibitory measure.
notes: Peddler/hawker licensing case; regulates itinerant selling, not lodging or boarding houses.

holding_summary: A testamentary devise in fee simple could not be validly restricted by a condition against alienation except by will, or against liability for the devisee's debts; such conditions are void as repugnant to the fee.
notes: Will construction/restraint on alienation of a fee simple estate; unrelated to letting or lodging.

holding_summary: In a personal-injury action, the court held it competent to show a boarding-house keeper's business profits as a measure of earning capacity, but there was insufficient evidence of the diminution in profits to submit that element of damages to the jury.
notes: Plaintiff's status as a 'boarding house keeper' arises only incidentally, as a fact bearing on loss-of-earning-capacity damages in a railroad negligence suit; the court does not address who occupied the house, duration, or legal character of any letting/boarding arrangement. Passing mention per spec §4; marked irrelevant.

holding_summary: In ejectment, evidence that defendant entered farmland under a parol gift, cleared and improved it, and paid taxes for over thirty years was sufficient to submit adverse possession to the jury, including constructive possession of the whole tract through a tenant occupying part of it.
notes: Ejectment/adverse possession of farmland based on a parol gift; tenant mentioned only re: constructive possession of farm fields, unrelated to lodging or room letting.

holding_summary: Whether a tenant holding over on a lease of a wall for advertising purposes remained liable for further years' rent, after the sign's view was obstructed and the tenant vacated, was properly submitted to the jury on the question of continued possession.
notes: Commercial lease of a wall for advertising signage, holdover-tenancy dispute; unrelated to dwelling/room occupancy.

holding_summary: Cotenants who for eight years treated a co-owner as a tenant in common despite a prior decree voiding his deed were estopped from denying his interest, and an outstanding title they acquired inured to his benefit as cotenant.
notes: Tenants-in-common title dispute over West Virginia timberland; unrelated to dwelling occupancy or lodging.

holding_summary: An accommodation indorser who paid a note included among debts secured by a creditors' collateral-pooling agreement was entitled to a pro rata share of the collateral proceeds, notwithstanding a clause purporting to limit the benefit to the original creditor.
notes: Principal-surety/subrogation dispute over creditor collateral; unrelated to letting or lodging.

holding_summary: Where a testator's spendthrift life-estate trusts for his sons remained valid despite the lapse of a charitable remainder for failure to comply with the statutory execution period, the life estates did not merge into the sons' resulting fee.
notes: Spendthrift trust/merger doctrine in estate administration; unrelated to dwelling letting.

holding_summary: A borough ordinance requiring a permit, fee, and bond before a water company could excavate streets to lay pipe was a reasonable police-power regulation for public safety and convenience, not an unlawful burden on the company's franchise.
notes: Municipal regulation of street excavation permits for a water utility; unrelated to lodging/boarding house regulation.

holding_summary: A fire insurance policy's vacancy clause barred recovery where a new, never-before-tenanted dwelling built for sale became vacant again after a period of occupancy and so remained for more than ten days before the fire.
notes: Fire insurance vacancy-clause dispute over a new spec-built house; occupancy discussed only in the insurance-vacancy sense, not compensated letting to lodgers/tenants for pay.
